account:
Today I inspected the mill's stall stock: two stacks of 64 hay bales, offered at two emeralds each. I have not established their quality. I kept my lunch and council-letter appointments, though no council letters have been handed to the secretary or me. My next appointment is tea at the east-bank dockside cottage at fifteen hundred.

The unusual matter is the repeated rumor of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' I heard that phrase from Townsfolk 01, 12, and 22, but none supplied concrete details or an original source. Yesterday the innkeeper denied proposing such a change and traced his information only to Townsfolk 03. I cannot tell whether this is a real proposal or merely a rumor circulating among neighbors. The bakery appears to be the place to inquire, not necessarily the source or organizer. Builder says the baker is now at the nearby market stall, but I have not yet obtained the baker's account.

Builder has completed the authorized Bridge and Landing Survey and delivered it to the secretary. Both report no specific damage; the secretary says the crossings worked and the report is not structural certification. I have requested the written report for review and intend to pay the agreed two emeralds. This survey was an inspection, not permission to alter the crossings. Its fee and the book expense are to be recorded separately. The secretary has preserved my original appointments and has been helping with records and inquiries. I have no evidence that either she or builder is concealing a proposal. The purpose of any actual bridge or port change remains unknown; so far I have no verified plan, organizer, or repair need.
